newsitem.title: POLAND: Security bureau accuses Walesa over secret papers.
newsitem.headline: Security bureau accuses Walesa over secret papers.

text.p: Poland's State Security Bureau (UOP) has formally accused ex-president Lech Walesa of illegally keeping secret documents, a crime which could incur three years in jail, prosecutors said on Tuesday.
Ryszard Kucinski, spokesman for the Warsaw prosecutor's office, told Reuters that his office would investigate the bureau's complaint.

"It concerns this, that Lech Walesa, as president, received materials from the Interior Ministry and the UOP which were covered by the secrecy rule and after his term finished he did not return these materials," Kucinski said.

He gave no details but said the article of the criminal code cited by the bureau "says that anyone whoever hides or removes a document which he does not have the right to hold infringes regulations and risks three years imprisonment."

The security bureau's charge coincided with a renewed debate over allegations, made at the end of Walesa's presidential term, that his ex-communist foe Jozef Oleksy, then prime minister, had long informed for Moscow spies.

Military prosecutors subsequently dropped an inquiry into Oleksy, saying the evidence was too weak and flawed, and the government this week published what it said was a full collection of the secret documents on the case.

Walesa's former presidential spokesman, Marek Karpinski, told Reuters he personally speculated that the UOP move might have been steered by the ruling ex-communists to divert attention from the politically-embarrassing Oleksy issue.

Under rules laid down by Walesa's predecessor Wojciech Jaruzelski, he said, an outgoing president's office had three months to dispose of secret documents after which the remainder were destroyed. "Maybe that happened in this case," he said.
Walesa, who as Solidarity chief led the Soviet bloc's first free trade union to its 1989 victory over communism, could not immediately be reached for comment.
Walesa lost elections last year to ex-communist Aleksander Kwasniewski and ended his five years as president in December.
